learning: Across five iterations, every controller change (kp 2.5 to 3.0, kd 0.05 to 0.1, ki 0.05 to 0.3) and every geometry change left max_error within about 0.007 m of 0.065. If speed also fails to move it, the limit is probably the start-up or early-bend response rather than any tunable gain. The next controller test would then be base_speed 1.4, to see whether lower speed at the bends reduces the drift.
notes: Complete package for the Builder's wheel_radius 0.035 m test. Controller is unchanged from iteration 4, so the race isolates drivetrain speed. The Builder's sensor layout, footprint, body and mass are kept.
rationale: The Builder's geometry (wheel_radius 0.035 m, sensors at x = -0.03 to 0.03 m and y = 0.04 m, sensor_size 0.012 m, body 0.18 x 0.12 m, mass 0.6 kg, track 0.12 m) is valid against the contract. Iterations 0 to 4 all ended off-track with max_error between 0.061 and 0.069, one line-loss event per track, and progress of 0.10 to 0.15. Controller changes have not moved that result. Raising kp from 2.5 to 3.0 with kd 0.05 to 0.1 (iterations 0 to 1) changed max_error by under 0.001 m. Raising ki from 0.05 to 0.3 with the 12 mm footprint (iteration 4, 50.1218) reproduced iteration 1 almost exactly: oval 0.0615, s-bend 0.0691, slalom 0.0687. So the integral term is not cancelling a bias, and the footprint is not the limit. The Builder's test is wheel_radius 0.035 m, which raises ground speed for the same PWM. To keep that test clean I change nothing in the controller. I keep the iteration 4 gains (kp 3.0, ki 0.3, kd 0.1), base_speed 1.6, last_direction line loss and the five-weight signal [-2,-1,0,1,2], so any change in progress or max_error is attributable to wheel_radius. ki 0.3 is kept, not reverted, because it showed no harm and reverting would add a confound. Expected behaviour: progress rises with speed, and max_error stays below about 0.069. If it rises, speed is increasing drift.
